item.title: Nori 1.14.0
item.description:
Nori brings Issues to Pro, creates pull and merge requests from Reviews and runs CI from the Checks tab. Text across the app now reads at 4.5:1 or more, in light and dark.
### Added
- Issues, with Pro: read, search and create GitHub and GitLab issues, comment with `@` and `#` completion, set labels and assignees, close or reopen, and *Start work* on a branch named after the issue. - Create a pull or merge request from Reviews: choose both branches and open it as a draft if you like. ⌘N in Reviews opens the form. - Drop a branch on another, or on HEAD, in the sidebar or the graph to open *Create Pull Request* (*Merge Request* on GitLab) with both branches filled in. - Control CI from a review's Checks tab: read job logs, live on GitLab, cancel a run, start a manual job, a pipeline or a workflow, and approve or reject a GitHub deployment. - Send Feedback: rate Nori out of five and add a comment for support, from Settings ▸ Feedback, the Help menu or a banner shown after a week of use. Leave your email only if you want a reply. - Click a linked worktree in the sidebar to see what it changed since its base (its request's target, else origin's default branch), uncommitted work included, then push it and open its pull or merge request. - Each agent's worktree in the sidebar shows its lines added and removed and how far it is ahead of and behind its base, kept current as the agent works.
### Changed
- Settings is a full-window page with a navigation rail instead of a sheet, and the repository stays as you left it beneath. - The right panel is always docked beside the graph: clicking a commit or the working copy swaps its content in place, and ◨ or ⌥⌘I shows or hides it. - A calmer look: lighter type weights, colour kept for actions, quieter avatars and ref chips in the graph, and polished Issues, Reviews, Settings, dialogs and toolbar panels. - Words on coloured pills and badges, branch names in their lane colour and field placeholders now read at 4.5:1 or more; a selected Issues or Reviews row takes the selection's colours. - Settings ▸ Appearance previews the open repository's three latest commits, with their authors' avatars. - Auto-merge uses the repository's default merge method without asking, and a refusal shows beside the button. - On the last conflicted file of a merge, the button reads *Mark resolved and commit merge*: it commits the merge, as it always did, and now says so.
### Fixed
- A branch pushed under another name, or renamed after its first push, shows as pushed in the graph, paired with its upstream. - A request shows as merged once its merge completes, even when it finishes later or outside Nori. - On GitLab, a failing job that is allowed to fail no longer blocks the merge when pipelines need not succeed. - Moving the pointer off an unfolded commit subject in the graph no longer leaves its shadow behind. - T3 Code worktrees in the sidebar show T3 Code and the thread's title again, instead of Claude Code and the first prompt. - On Windows and Linux, a repository opened through a symbolic link no longer marks its own branch as checked out in another worktree. - With files in conflict, *Show working copy* opens on the working copy that holds them, instead of on whatever commit was selected. - A pull refused because the branch and its remote both moved on now offers *Pull with rebase*, as a refused push already offered *Pull*. - Commands are named the same way everywhere: *Checkout this commit*, *Create branch here*, *Force push*, and the worktree sheet in sentence case. - On Windows and Linux, Drop stash in the stash panel's confirmation takes the first click, instead of it only closing the panel. - The toolbar's Undo names ⌘Z only while ⌘Z would do the same, and Settings › Shortcuts says it takes back what the undo notice offers. - In the Hunks presentation, Stage hunk and Unstage hunk move the whole hunk, instead of saying the selection holds no changed lines. - With Git in another language than English, a merge conflict now opens the resolver instead of reading as a failed command, and failed sign-ins and network errors are named again. - On Windows and Linux, the confirmation that removes a worktree dims the sheet behind it instead of blacking it out. - Issues' connect screen says it lists the repository's issues, not its pull requests. - The overview counts 1 branch and 1 contributor in the singular, and a dialog's close cross is named Close rather than a second Cancel. - While a merge, rebase or cherry-pick waits for you, its disabled buttons, History's Undo and the AI message button say to finish or abort it, instead of "Another Git command is running". - On Windows and Linux, screen readers read a shortened branch name whole in the new branch panel and the rebase banner, instead of split in two. - On Windows and Linux, screen readers read each interactive rebase step as its action and commit, stashes as a list, and each Stage button with its file. - Windows and Linux: the graph loads past its first 500 commits, and the automatic fetch runs again. - Unstaging in a repository without a first commit, and the fallbacks of stash pop and discard, work when the system language is not English. - The resolver's key hints say *yours* and *incoming* during a merge, and *Continue* says what it does for each operation. - Branch names Git refuses, `HEAD` among them, are caught as you type, and History shortens `Reset to` hashes. - Codex shows as signed in without repeating its own status line.
### Security
- An automatic fetch no longer runs a program the repository's own Git settings name, nor its hooks: opening a downloaded folder cannot run code unasked. *Fetch* in the toolbar still runs them. - GitLab images hosted on other sites show as links instead of loading, so their host cannot see when you read an issue or a merge request. - Clone refuses `fd::` and `ext::` addresses: one ran a command, the other hung for an hour. - Opening a repository runs none of its hooks, and links in forge comments open only when they are `http`, `https` or `mailto`. - Removing a worktree deletes only what Git removes: a crafted worktree entry can no longer get another folder deleted. - Codex runs with its shell, plugins, MCP servers and web search off when Nori asks it for text. - On Windows and Linux, the updater installs only a newer build signed for its version, and *Open in Default App* reveals file types it does not know instead of opening them.

item.title: Nori 1.13.0
item.description:
Nori adds first launch onboarding, reflog recovery, and a faster way to find repositories and manage reviews. Issues and Reviews now show more results, clearer permissions and progress, with better paging for large lists.
### Added
- First launch helps you find and open repository folders. - History can show reflog entries and restore a previous repository state. - Reviews shows merge progress and required thread resolutions, and the branch toolbar shows the stash count. - Press ⌘F (Ctrl+F on Windows and Linux) to search repositories; edit palette filters as you type.
### Changed
- Issues and Reviews load more results as you page through lists, and Reviews shows which actions your permissions allow. - Review lists refresh their previews and align timeline markers with comment authors.
### Fixed
- Large GitHub and GitLab review changes load without truncating their patches. - Offline forge calls retry, and redundant pushes are skipped.

item.title: Nori 1.12.1
item.description:
Reviews renders Markdown and shows people by their name; Windows and Linux get fixes to the menu, the command palette and blurred text.
### Added
- Reviews renders descriptions and comments as Markdown, with lists, tables and links, and the description can be edited from Overview when the forge allows it. - Reviews shows people by the name on their forge profile instead of their login, which stays on hover; the list search matches either.
### Fixed
- *Merge*, *Rebase* and *Rebase interactive* are greyed out on the checked-out branch's own menu. - In a review, ↻ also reloads the diff's discussions, so a comment posted on the forge appears without reopening the request. - On Windows and Linux, the application menu's commands can be clicked again, and saving one file repeatedly no longer reloads the whole repository. - On Windows and Linux, opening the command palette at a zoom other than 100 % no longer leaves an empty window. - On Linux, History and Overview text is sharp again when the system scales text, such as GNOME at 120 %.

item.title: Nori 1.12.0
item.description:
Nori now runs on Windows and Linux, with the same history, diffs, Reviews and Pro as on the Mac. Nothing changes on the Mac in this release.
### Added
- Nori for Windows 10 and 11 on x64: one installer, which asks whether to install Nori for everyone or only for you. - Nori for Linux on x86-64: `.deb`, `.rpm` and AppImage packages, for Ubuntu 22.04 or Debian 12 and newer, and current Fedora releases. - On Windows and Linux, Settings ▸ Updates offers each new version and installs it, as on the Mac. - Pro, the 14-day Pro trial and *Activate in Nori* work on Windows and Linux with the same License. - On Windows and Linux, a missing GitHub CLI, GitLab CLI or AI command-line tool links to its official installation guide.

item.title: Nori 1.11.0
item.description:
Nori is free: every Git feature works without an account, a Trial or a License. Reviews becomes Pro, with a 14-day trial on request.
### Added
- Without Pro, Reviews shows what it does and offers *Start 14-day Pro trial*, *Buy Pro* or a License Key; it contacts no forge until Pro is unlocked. - After buying Pro on the website, *Activate in Nori* on the confirmation page unlocks Pro on this Mac without typing a License Key.
### Changed
- Settings ▸ License shows Free, Pro trial with its days left, or Pro. Every existing License includes Pro. - *Push & Pull Request* stays free; without Pro, the created request opens in your browser instead of Reviews. - Every Mac is offered every update, with or without a License. - Starting a Pro trial or activating a License no longer asks for a name for your Mac or for marketing consent. - Reviews connects a repository to your account on its own when there is only one possible match.
### Removed
- Read-Only Mode and the Start 14-day Trial banner: no licence state limits a Git operation any more. - The *Unlock Nori* button in the title bar; a running Pro trial still counts its days there.
### Fixed
- Reviews stays inside the window at its smallest size, at 100 % and at 150 % zoom.

item.title: Nori 1.10.0
item.description:
Nori is now signed and notarized by Apple, so it opens without the Open Anyway step.
### Added
- ⌘-click a relative import in a diff to open that file: changed files open in their diff, the others in a full-file preview. - Open a worktree in your selected editor from its context menu in the sidebar. - Settings ▸ License offers Unlock Nori… or Buy Nori… when you have no License, so the title-bar badge is no longer the only way in. - Dragging a commit or branch tip on the graph draws a tether to the pointer and glides it onto the drop target. - Syntax themes and code fonts preview in Settings ▸ Diff as you move through the menus; nothing is saved until you pick one. - Nori offers to move itself to Applications when it runs from a place where it cannot update, such as straight from the disk image.
### Changed
- The update window shows the notes of every version between yours and the update. - Review diffs scroll as one continuous surface across files, with discussions inline. - ✦ A usage-limit or spend-cap refusal from your AI CLI is explained, with a hint to retry or switch tool. - Buy Nori opens Checkout directly after a Trial, with no second email link, and the unlock sheet says where the verification link went. - Graph lanes start at their branch tips, and commit details align the author's picture with their name.
### Fixed
- Unstaging and discarding in a repository with no first commit work again with Git 2.54, which words its error differently.

item.title: Nori 1.9.0
item.description:
### Added
- Choose the code font, size and ligatures for file diffs, blame and the inline conflict resolver in Settings ▸ Diff. Nori includes familiar monospaced fonts and can use fonts installed on this Mac. - Show author pictures in History and commit details, with initials as the fallback. Settings ▸ Appearance offers None, Initials and Avatar; pictures load only when Avatar is selected.
### Changed
- The ambient background follows the open repository's marker color, with a smooth transition when switching repositories.

item.title: Nori 1.8.1
item.description:
### Fixed
- Buying Nori from the app unlocks this Mac at once: no License Key to paste, no second email.

item.title: Nori 1.8.0
item.description:
Nori holds a fifth of the memory it did: on git/git (82,000 commits), 99 MB at rest instead of 523 MB.
### Changed
- The sidebar builds only the branch and tag rows on screen: −180 MB on a repository with 1,000 tags. - The diff page loads when a diff is about to open and is released 3 minutes after the last one closes: no WebKit process until then, −120 MB at rest. - The ambient background is drawn from small images (−80 MB), and the History graph keeps its colours and edges in a fraction of the space (−50 MB on wide graphs). - The app is 31 MB installed instead of 57, and an 11 MB download instead of 14.
### Fixed
- Updating no longer asks for keychain access several times at launch: licensing state lives in a private file, and this update asks at most once.

item.title: Nori 1.7.3
item.description:
### Fixed
- The title bar counts the Trial's days left instead of showing Unlock Nori, and shows nothing once a License is active. - Pushing to the remote's default branch no longer offers to open a pull request.

item.title: Nori 1.7.2
item.description:
### Fixed
- Start 14-day Trial stays offered after Nori's first licence check; it used to disappear on a new Mac. - No more Renew links: every update is included with a License.

item.title: Nori 1.7.1
item.description:
### Changed
- Nori starts a 14-day free Trial on first launch, then needs a License: US$40 once, two Macs, every update included. - While purchases are not open yet, Buy says so instead of reporting an error.

item.title: Nori 1.7.0
item.description:
✦ AI explains commits and diffs, proposes conflict resolutions and summarises requests for review; ⌘K searches the whole history; branches and commits drag and drop. This release also closes the data-loss and security issues found before the public launch.
### Added
- ✦ Explain for a commit or a diff (whole file or one hunk), ✦ Suggest resolution per conflict hunk, and ✦ Summarise for review in Reviews ▸ Overview (never posted); per-use switches and a shared Max context size in Settings ▸ AI. - History search in ⌘K across the whole history, with `author:`, `path:`, `content:`, `regex:`, `before:`, `after:`, `between:` and `hash:` filters, a calendar and value completion; *Show only these in the graph* filters History, 200 per page up to 10,000. - File history (⌘⇧H, 100 commits per page up to 2,000, across renames) and blame (⌘⇧B). - Drag and drop of branches and commits in the sidebar and the graph: merge, rebase, new branch, cherry-pick, revert or push at the drop point. - Checks: a summary bar, required checks listed as Expected, annotations that open their line, GitLab trigger jobs, *Re-run job* and *Re-run failed jobs*, a 30 s refresh while running, counts on the list badge and in the Push menu. - An External editor setting (Xcode, VS Code, Cursor, Zed, Sublime Text, Nova, BBEdit, JetBrains IDEs, any app): *Open in <editor>* ⌘⇧E and *Open Repository in <editor>* ⌃⌥E. - App-wide zoom, ⌘+ and ⌘− from 80 to 150 %, kept across relaunches. - File ▸ Open Repository… and Open Recent; a folder dropped on the Dock icon or given to `open -a Nori` opens as a repository. - Nori ▸ Check for Updates…, release notes in the update window, and a Help menu: website, release notes, Report an Issue (on GitHub), keyboard shortcuts, diagnostic report, privacy policy and terms. - Acknowledgements for the open-source software Nori includes, in About Nori. - Recent crash and hang reports in the exported diagnostic report; nothing is sent.
### Changed
- Nori's bundle identifier is now `app.meetnori.nori` (was `com.nori.desktop`): settings, tabs and recent repositories carry over; macOS asks again for notifications and folder access. - Nori checks for updates automatically, once a day, unless Settings ▸ Updates turns it off; installing stays your call. - ✦ AI tools run in a private empty folder with their tools off, never inside the repository. - Git and its hooks get the login shell's PATH, proxies and SSH agent: nvm, volta, asdf, mise, fnm and MacPorts tools resolve as in Terminal. - Automatic fetch gives way to anything you start, waits until the last fetch is one interval old, backs off up to an hour after failures and never posts a notification. - Quitting while a push, rebase or other Git action runs asks first. - A push refused because the remote has someone else's commits offers Pull, which rebases your commits on theirs, not Force push. - Errors stay on screen until dismissed with ✕ or esc. - Settings ▸ Shortcuts lists every shortcut, and ⌘K shows the keys the menus actually bind. - Reviews says comments are public as soon as you send them, in the composer and in Submit Review. - Reviews offers `glab` for GitLab remotes and `gh` for GitHub, connects every signed-in account (github.com and Enterprise side by side), says Merge Request on GitLab, and binds a remote only to an identity on its host, starting on `upstream`. - Push & PR from a fork with an `upstream` remote opens the request on the parent; on a GitLab remote it reads Push & MR. - Merging asks first when commits were pushed after you opened the request. - Reviews waits for a spent rate limit to reset, and backs off up to 15 minutes after repeated failures. - Merge bar: Checks block only on required checks the forge names; Approvals count against the required number, `1 of 2`. - The Checks tab lists failures first with completion times; GitHub checks are read up to a thousand; GitLab manual jobs count as neutral; Origin says checks are unavailable. - An Overview contributor click adds that author to the History filter. - Stash is back in the top bar, beside Branch: its panel pops, applies or drops a saved stash even with a clean working copy. - Git 2.36 is the minimum version.
### Removed
- Removed syntax colouring for Ada, AutoHotkey v2, gnuplot, nginx, Org and Racket files, and the Aurora X theme: their grammars are GPL-licensed. Those files show as plain text.
### Fixed
- Fixed ✦ actions running a repository's own Claude Code hooks, settings and MCP servers. - Fixed Push & PR publishing a file outside the repository when a pull request template was a symbolic link. - Fixed Open in Default App running scripts, apps and installers from a repository; they open as text or in Finder. - Fixed Force push overwriting commits a background fetch had brought in. - Fixed the branch menu's Push sending a branch started from `origin/main` into `main`, and the upstream dialog offering to delete `origin/main`. - Fixed interactive rebase dropping commits made after its plan opened. - Fixed checkout of a deleted branch wiping edits to a file of the same name, stash Drop, Pop and Apply acting on the wrong stash, and remote branch deletion removing commits pushed since your last fetch. - Fixed a branch being deleted when its Undo snapshot could not be saved. - Fixed Undo snapshots, discarded untracked files included, leaving the machine with `git push --mirror` and showing in `git log --all`: they now live outside the repository, existing ones move there when it opens, and those of repositories never reopened go after 31 days. - Fixed stage and discard acting on the wrong file when a repository's subfolder was opened. - Fixed empty diffs and failed partial staging under Git's `color.ui`, `diff.noprefix` or `apply.whitespace`. - Fixed a commit or push hanging when a hook left a background process running. - Fixed blame on file names outside ASCII. - Fixed unknown SSH hosts, an unaccepted Xcode license and missing Command Line Tools being reported as credential failures. - Fixed Reviews listing only the first 100 files of a GitHub pull request; up to 3,000 now. - Fixed a lost connection leading to a comment, reply, review or merge being sent twice: Nori offers *Check if posted*. - Fixed Reviews' Forget keeping the account's cached data and reconnecting it at the next scan. - Fixed Reviews and Push & PR for SSH remotes using a `~/.ssh/config` alias or a non-standard SSH port. - Fixed one unreadable item (SAML, a missing token permission) blanking a whole Reviews screen. - Fixed an unreadable Reviews store locking Reviews out: it is set aside and a fresh one opens. - Fixed the open request no longer refreshing after Nori came back from the background, and a hidden tab's Reviews still polling. - Fixed "Reconnect required" staying after signing in again, and a new sign-in waiting 30 s after a 401. - Fixed GitLab conversations showing the oldest 50 discussions, GitLab lists stopping at 100 requests, and GitHub Changes and Commits stopping at 100. - Fixed Origin accounts never connecting. - Fixed files with an empty diff showing a loading skeleton forever. - Fixed a crash expanding context in GitLab files with accented names. - Fixed the status bar tooltip showing credentials stored in a remote URL. - Fixed the diff surface keeping every document it drew in memory, and closed tabs staying in memory. - Fixed home screen errors not showing, and "git not found" flashing at launch. - Fixed tabs on a disconnected drive being forgotten at launch. - Fixed VoiceOver reading shortcut symbols as part of button names. - Fixed the notification permission prompt appearing at first launch.
